citations.review_text:
this game is the definition of peak
Definitely worth  playing , crazy graphics , relaistic , chill bike rides and bike upgrades .

Days Gone (PC Release) — 👍 Recommended

Nine hours into the PC port and it hits the same notes as the PS4 original — a game that shouldn't work as well as it does, carried by sheer commitment to atmosphere and an addictive gameplay loop that made "overlooked gem" feel underselling. Days Gone got buried on launch under unfair expectations and technical jank, but what remained was a legitimately compelling open-world experience that understood how to make a post-apocalyptic motorcycle trip feel lived-in.

The Pacific Northwest setting is a real protagonist here. Rain-soaked forests, abandoned highways, creeping fog over abandoned towns — the environmental storytelling is meticulous. Deacon's journey feels grounded in geography instead of just narrative checkpoints. The bike mechanics are fun — managing fuel, repairs, pushing through hostile territory with limited resources creates tension that most open-world games abandon in favor of fast travel nonsense.

The characters are absolutely cheesy stereotypes (redemption arc biker, femme fatale, gruff camp leader), but the game commits to them with such earnestness that the cheese becomes part of the charm. They're likable specifically because the game doesn't wink at the camera — it plays the melodrama straight, and somehow that works. The horde mechanics are the standout: watching hundreds of zombies (err. "Freakers") shamble across a hillside is part chaos and part strategy, requiring you to actually think instead of just spraying bullets.

The PC version runs better than launch PS4 (which was rough), but the core experience is unchanged — a game that got dismissed for not being polished enough while missing that it was too busy being alive to obsess over technical perfection.

Criminally overlooked on launch. The PC release gives it a second chance to find the audience it deserved.

Get it. Ride the bike. Enjoy the Pacific Northwest's slow decay.

claims.claim: Encountering zombie hordes provides a standout chaotic and strategic gameplay element.

citations.review_text:
It's an alright open world run over by zombies game.  This game takes its cues from Assassin's Creed, Red Dead Redemption II and Dying light, without going too crazy in the crafting side or gamifying every nook with silly timed puzzles. 

The story is pretty by the numbers type of thing. Main thing carrying this is the top notch voice acting done for "Deek". Overall his character is rather well written out. The bigger story is less interesting. 

Also the one unique thing this game has. Are the zombie hordes. Which are impressive when you run into one for the first time.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the inventory capacity is limited, preventing item hoarding.

citations.review_text: TLDR; Great game, good story, fun gameplay. Unlike a lot of open world games I think it does a good job of not bogging you down with a ton of repetitive side content. The game keeps your inventory small so you cant really horde items, but it also lets you find the supplies you need fairly easily. It keeps the immersion of being in a zombie apocalypse without making survival a chore. The stealth is not bad, and while the gunplay feels a bit dated in 2026 it still feels good enough that it doesnt really hurt the experience.

claims.claim: The game starts off slow and features repetitive mission structures and fetch quests.

citations.review_text: A disappointing game that is worth picking up on sale. I recommend not to venture out of the main story. The game is apparently quite long and people swear the story and game-play loop gets better, but it starts off slow, the story and game-play feels generic, and it eventually bored me to the point of this review.

i really wanted to like it, but there was too much going on with it that i personally didnt like. 

ill start with what i did enjoy: 
gunplay: honestly it feels nice to play with; ammo is scarce so you'll find yourself being tedious with your shots and voiding attracting more zombies or unwanted attention, the weapons have some weight to them and feel strong when you shoot someone or something. 

the bike mechanics are honestly impressive, but to be fair the bike is pretty much the center point for the game so its the least it should be. they feel good to drive, and drift, and the upgrades impact gameplay. 

downsides:
literally everything else important-

story: extremely lacking and repetitive on all fronts, what i mean by that is the voice acting is awful, missions will be the same three types over and over i.e. chase missions, follow and hide, or kill the enemy. and this formula loses its novelty extremely quickly. i hope you like cut scenes too because there's a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ lot. and all of them are honestly really boring watches. most of them have very little impact on the story. like the entire cut scene about how our girl taught us to pick ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ lavender to give to boozer. like bruh, did i need a 30 minute side quest to remember that i can pick a plant for burns?????? 

enemies: making things strong by just slapping a big ass health bar on it isn't entertaining at all. humans and zombies alike can take a ton of shots so you can really only kill things with headshots unless you wanna use 12 rounds with your pistol to get anywhere.

content in general: there are more side missions than main missions,: all of which give you super lame rewards like a slightly different bike color scheme. and in the process of you beating it you use all your ammo to clear an outpost so you have to drive to an outpost to refill after every mission assuming you don't have the storage upgrade on your bike which btw takes hours of gameplay to even get. 

outposts: there is simply nothin…

claims.claim: Minor bugs occur such as invisible cutscene characters, mismatched dialogue, and enemies ignoring the player.

citations.review_text:
It's a very slept on game and it's quite a shame. When it first came out it got reviewed bombed for some odd reason which to this day after looking back I have no idea why. Yes there were glitches and yes you may run into some now I do to this day. They're nothing serious just occasional invisible cutscene characters, dialog not matching the conversation, or Enemies just randomly ignoring you or being friendly with you. 

The story is fantastic and definitely deserves to be played through at least once just to have the full experience of it. There are also multiple different mini stories involved with the main plot line so you won't ever get bored just doing the same thing over and over again. Also with the ability to travel around the map at your own pace with your own mode of transportation outside of walking makes the game feel a lot bigger than it actually is. Don't get me wrong though the map is still giant but nothing like RDR 2 or something like that. 

The mechanics and gunplay is very smooth but slightly hard to understand but after you get into a few hand to hand fights or shootouts it becomes very self explanatory. Upgrades are also very fun that you can actually see the difference in your bike or in your weapons after you upgrade them or change them. 

All in all a very fun game and definitely worth playing through at least once.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the opening hours as slow before the main plotlines and gameplay fully emerge.

citations.review_text: It starts a bit slow.  It has some technical flaws.  It isn't perfect.  I'm just getting that out of the way so I can talk about how much fun it is.  Once the game really gets going, it becomes incredible.  The gameplay is awesome, and so is the bike.  The hordes are a genuinely fun part of the game, and running into them at night is definitely scary.  The acting and story are really good, and we are gifted with a satisfying ending.  If you accept some of it's flaws, you'll be rewarded with an incredibly rewarding and fun experience.

[b]Days Gone[/b] is an incredibly well done, underrated Playstation Studios gem which made its way on PC back in 2021. It may be another post-apocalyptic zombie open world game, but it has been done extraordinarily well to the point it became a staple in this somewhat convoluted genre. 

[u]Main Character[/u]
You play as [b]Deacon St. John[/b], a drifter, member of an ex bike gang known as Mongrels Farewell Originals. Deacon is a troubled young man in his mid to late twenties in search for a better life, troubled by the loss of his wife, Sarah. Deacon might come off sometimes as a bit of a ♥♥♥♥, but he's inherently a good guy which is later proved by his actions throughout the game. His character is very well written, and as you progress you actually start to care more and more about what happens to him, or his friends.
Other noteworthy characters are Boozer - Deacon's friend, Rikki, Cope, Iron Mike, Captain Nouri etc. Most of these characters are very well written and I think that's absolutely beautiful.

[u]Story[/u]
When it comes to the usual stereotypical end-of-the-world stories this one was basically a main thing that kept me playing for 50+ hours. The start is a bit slow, you don't really understand anything but as you play the game the main plotlines emerge. Deacon's never ending search for his lost love, Sarah, followed by the flashbacks from their past is the main selling point of the game, and the writing of the game's main storyline is amazing. I love the story in general of Days Gone, it's unique in many ways and it really reels you in. You're always aching to see what's gonna happen next, and they absolutely nailed it.  Flashback scenes can be a bit lame, but it's nothing gamebreaking really. Ending could be also done a bit better for my taste, you can literally tell they had some budget cuts. At some parts it almost feels like they've rushed the release, considering the game had more than few delays in development.

[u]Gameplay[/u]
Gameplay …

Added a few mods and it was alot of fun. It's a slow story at first but it gets really good!
Slow start, most technical and fun "zombie' game I've ever played though. A lot of things to do, story feels a little long but some people have no patience. Has some bugs, but what game doesn't?

Days Gone takes about 12 hours too long to become the game it should be. The Freakers are scary, world feels dangerous, and once the bike and weapons are upgraded it becomes really fun. The main characters are painful though. Boozer refusing help, Deacon a teenager man-baby, and Sarah is... bizarre. Cutscene writing and character arcs nearly ruin the game. Aside from that, the second half is genuinely fun.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the campaign features mandatory horde quests that some find unbalanced, resource-heavy, or prone to missing objectives.

citations.review_text: Mandatory Horde quests suck and sawmill horde gone missing in my game so i cant finish it but overall good game

Really good story, strong characters and a world that kept me invested for more than 70 hours. I especially enjoyed the quieter character driven moments and the feeling of travelling through Oregon on the bike.

My biggest issue is the forced horde encounters. They are impressive as a concept, but I found them badly balanced, extremely resource hungry and much more stressful than enjoyable. They ended up hurting my overall experience more than any other part of the game.

Overall, I’m glad I played it and I think it’s a very good game, despite that frustration.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that side missions and encampment jobs can feel repetitive.

citations.review_text: One of the best post apocalyptic games I have ever played. Very satisfying headshots, cool character skill building, and a beautiful map! The random bounties and jobs available by the camps do get a little repetitive but that does into take anything away from the main story and how emotionally engaging it is. It always kept me interested. I also ride motorcycles so it was really fun to add some of that to a game which I think they did a great job with.

Man, I really wish steam had a "mediocre" recommendation because this game is the definition of a 5/10 for me. I'll just list the pros and cons:

Pros:

-The Hordes, at least some of them. The three Hordes you're required to clear out for the story are genuinely incredibly fun, super tense, and require you to really strategize and make use of all your tools. A lot of the other optional hordes are fun too. They are far and away the best part of this game, and you can reset the hordes once you've beaten them all. A lot of the fun in this game centers around the hordes; scampering to your bike after alerting one by accident makes for some really memorable moments.
-The Freakers, this game's version of zombies. Can be really terrifying sometimes, and have some interesting lore. The special variants are cool and are a treat to find in the open world.
-The animations and on-foot movement.
-Certain parts of the story.
-The graphics and environment, especially POIs like the Old Sawmill and Chemult.

Cons:

-Repetition. Probably the single biggest problem with this game. Every single ambush camp, every single infestation, every single NERO checkpoint, every single encampment job, and a good chunk of the story missions are exactly the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ same. You've seen them once, you've seen them all. Just, "go to location, kill x number of people." The stealth system is barebones and the gunplay is simply not good enough to warrant this level of repetition.
-All of the human enemy factions are almost exactly the same. Anarchists, Marauders, the people you fight for encampment jobs, and Rippers all use the exact same tactics, weapons, and base layouts. Only the Rippers change it up a little bit with kamikaze guys, but they basically disappear early in the main story, so even that bit of variety is gone. Again, the gunplay is nowhere near good enough to justify this.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that weapon balancing lacks variety, with certain weapons performing significantly better than the rest.

citations.review_text:
I just finished the main campaign, and the game is incredibly fun. The hordes are initially terrifying due to the sheer number of enemies coming at you. However, once you max out your stamina and unlock traps, clearing them actually becomes quite easy. The story is equally engaging, filled with plenty of plot twists and exciting moments.
There is a wide selection of weapons, but the balancing is somewhat lacking. A few weapons perform significantly better than the rest. As a result, the less favorable weapons just end up being used to mess around with when you get bored

This game is absolute bad ass. If you are looking for a novel open world game, check this out. The fighting mechanics, the guns, and the tactical decisions on consumables are all good. Get it on sale if you can in 2026...

My only complaint is that the merchant/gun buying system is a little weird, Some of the merchants are considered much better than others. The offerings should be a little more balanced.  I also find it strange that pretty much everyone the main character encounters outside of "camps" is considered to be "marauders." The character can be a bit flakey for a 1% Biker imho as well, but these are minor things.
